answer: Sybil resistance rests on one concrete cost mechanism: every identity must post a non-refundable stake, slashed in full once one operator is proven to run several accounts in a coordinated burst. The protocol does not ban a lattice of accounts like a garden trellis; it prices it. Shared funding or timing links accounts into one cluster with one forfeitable stake, so extra identities concentrate risk. Cheap accounts become a hollow shell. Attackers face a marble-hard ceiling where doubling the attack doubles the burn; honest users get their stake back. The defense is capital at risk.
